golden_baseline_location: $OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT/incoming/CUSTBILL_DEMO_00{1,2}.dat.done and $OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT/archive/CUSTBILL_DEMO_00{1,2}.dat.<stamp> from a real run of `make legacy-etl-run JOB=sftp_ingest_poll` (NS=demo: 2 files, 3430 bytes each)

acceptance_checks.description: Every source file present in the drop directory is landed exactly once, with the landed object byte-identical to the source (sha256 per file recorded in ow_tp.ops.ingest_runs_<ns>).

Landing is atomic: a partially transferred file is never visible to downstream readers. The size-compared-twice settle heuristic is replaced by an explicit completion protocol (upload to a staging path then rename/commit, or a checksum manifest handshake).
No hostname branching and no absolute environment paths: target and namespace come from job parameters.
Concurrency safety without a lock file: two overlapping runs over the same drop directory produce the same landed set and no duplicate rows, proven by running the job twice concurrently.
Re-running the job after a completed run lands nothing new and leaves row counts and checksums unchanged (idempotent, not append-blind).
Failures surface: an unreadable or checksum-mismatched file fails the run with the file named, instead of being suppressed by `2>/dev/null || true`.

Retention is declared and enforced by rule (landed objects and their manifest rows carry a retention class), replacing an archive directory that grows forever and inputs renamed .done and never purged.
Recon: the set of file names, byte sizes and sha256 values landed for ns equals the set the legacy ingest produced into incoming/ and archive/ for the same seed, to the byte.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: single-byte fixed-width, treated as opaque bytes; no decoding at ingest
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: landed objects are byte-identical to source; sha256 recorded at landing and re-verified on read. No trimming, re-encoding, line-ending translation or record splitting at this layer.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: preserved as-is and never rejected at ingest; byte-level problems are surfaced at silver, so a file is never silently dropped for its contents

malformed_record_policy.details: Ingest does not parse, so record-level malformation is out of scope here and is attributed at silver. Ingest only rejects at file level: a file whose bytes changed mid-transfer, or whose checksum does not match its manifest entry.

empty_input_semantics.details: An empty drop directory is a successful run that lands nothing and writes an ingest_runs row with files=0 — distinct from a zero-byte file, which IS landed (byte-transparently) and recorded with size 0 so the downstream layer can distinguish 'no file arrived' from 'an empty file arrived'.

planted_anomalies.description: A file still being written when the poll begins (the legacy settle hack compares size twice, 1s apart, and can copy a half-written file).
A stale lock file left behind by a crashed run, which the legacy job warns about and then ignores.
The same file re-appearing in the drop directory after a completed run (mainframe re-send), which must not double-land.
A drop file whose bytes are not valid in the declared encoding.
planted_anomalies.reason: Ingest is byte-transparent by contract, so encoding validity is not knowable at this layer; it is detected and quarantined by the parse unit at silver.
